findings.quote: I added an extra second to the fall time
findings.note: The entry it points at is 'computing the total fall time t = 5 s and then reporting t squared as the percentage'. Nothing in it adds a second, and a six-second fall time would not produce that option at all, so the route describes an error the entry does not contain. A student who reported the square of the time has no route that fits, and one who did mis-count the seconds would be routed to the wrong option.
findings.fix: I gave the square of the fall time

findings.quote: I found the total fall time from the height
findings.note: Both non-distractor entries start from exactly this step - mistakes[0] needs t = 5 to form the difference of squares and mistakes[1] states it outright - so the phrase does not separate the right solver from the wrong ones. The step that does separate is taking the distance in the last second from the nth-second rule.
findings.fix: I used the nth second distance formula

notes: mistakes[0] typed calculation with route null accepted as a boundary: the route (difference of the distances at 5 s and 4 s) was right and the half-g factor was dropped, though the entry also mistakes the raw number for a percentage, which leans application; I would not fail it on the definition. mistakes[2] distractor flag looks honest - 64 and 40 are the near misses named and neither is 49. Numbers re-checked: t = 5 s, S5 = 45 m, 45/125 x 100 = 36; the two wrong values 9 and 25 also reproduce.
